mpn.why: W2 B2B (orchestrator decision, 07.11.2026): one hermaphroditic part on both boards instead of the QSH/QTH pair of W2 AREA (b2b.superseded). For QSH/QTH the land patterns are readable (Samtec Rev M drawings, b2b.superseded.src), but no first-party document states the QTH-over-QSH mating pin map, so the pin map would stay an owner action. The LSHM has an official KiCad 10.0.7 footprint that matches the Samtec Rev G drawing, a documented mating map (print Rev Z note 4, b2b.mating_map), a smaller courtyard (30.70 x 6.20 against 41.77 x 7.99 and 40.50 x 7.61) and one MPN for both halves. Cost: no ground plane, so every rail contact has its GND return beside it and the rail block is guarded by GND (guard_rule, W2 B2B review R2). 100 contacts (-150) against the 80 of LSHM-140 (candidate a80): (a) needs 69, 83 with the spare; the -150 keeps 17 contacts beyond the spare rule for nets that placement may add, the -140 takes the 69 but misses the spare rule (83 > 80); the -150 costs 0.003 of the PWR-A and 0.006 of the PWR-B ratio at 1.8 (MODEL ESTIMATE). Neither covers (b), which needs 119 contacts (143 with the spare): if the owner moves the switch groups to PWR-B, the B2B choice reopens. Two -02.5 halves give the 5.00 mm stack, so hA, the windows and the F45 standoffs stay. Stock is evidence only

mating_map.formula: pin n of J208 (PWR-A) meets pin n+1 of J209 (PWR-B) for n odd and pin n-1 for n even; the map is its own inverse

A bottom-side footprint flipped top/bottom, or flipped left/right and turned 180 degrees, is that mirror; pcb/check_boards.py b2b with pin_map from b2b-nets.json contacts checks it

b2b.pin_map_rule: pcb/prepare.py b2b_contacts (W2 B2B, review R2; sense pairs at the end since 11.11.2026): J208 column c = contacts 2c-1 (odd row) and 2c (even row). Each declared sense pair takes one column at the end of the strip (the last column, a further pair two columns before it), with a GND guard column before it. From contact 1 on the odd row: the rail block of guard_rule in the order rail_order, which lists the rail contacts one by one (a net listed once keeps its contacts together; unlisted rails after it, by name), each rail contact followed by its GND return on the same row; one GND guard after the rail block, in that row; the rails of rail_row_even the same way from contact 2 on the even row; the other crossing nets in name order on the free contacts of the even row, one per column, one contact each; the rest spare (nc in the graph). For (a) (since W2 GR-5B, when the six damper rail nodes and VBUS_LABPORT stopped crossing): odd 1-37 the 10 rail contacts (1, 5, ... 37) with their GND returns (3, 7, ... 39), 41 guard, even 2-14 the 4 LAB5 contacts (2, 6, 10, 14) with their GND returns (4, 8, 12, 16), even 18-60 the 22 signal nets, the other contacts up to 96 spare, 97-98 guard, 99-100 the LNA4 sense pair (until W2 GR-5B: odd 1-65 the 17 rail contacts with their returns to 67, 69 guard). J209 contact m carries the net of J208 contact b2b_mate(m). python -I pcb/write_b2b_graph.py writes the map into the graph refs (--check compares). Design value. Why the rails take one row and the sense pair the end: on the PWR-B board of record (build/kicad/boards/PWR_B/make_spec.py) J209 lies on the bottom side turned so that column 50 is under the ch4 shunt R246 and column 1 next to the end of the LAB5 trunk; the rail row faces the top-edge headers and the LNA channels, the signal row the harness headers J202/J203 below the strip, the LAB5 contacts sit next to the end of the trunk and the Kelvin pair reaches its shunt, as on the FX8 placeholder map that routed (rails mostly in one row, signals in the other). The checkerboard maps of 07-11.11.2026 (rails in both rows) left 3 to 15 connections open in route runs 43103920112, 43106418931, 43109754670, 43112965018 and 43115627813. b2b.rail_row_even_why: W2 B2B (11.11.2026): the four LAB5 contacts take the start of the even row (each followed by its GND return), so on the PWR-B board of record they sit in the J209 row that faces the LAB5 trunk below the strip and reach it by a via each and an F.Cu plate; above the strip the row of the other rails then has no LAB5 vias in the way of the rails that leave to the west (route runs 43118324282, 43119630792 and 43121336632 with LAB5 in the rail row left 2 to 4 of them open). Design value
b2b.guard_rule: W2 B2B review R2 (07.11.2026): the pads are 0.30 mm wide at 0.50 mm pitch, so neighbouring pads of a row are 0.20 mm apart (b2b.footprint, Samtec Rev G), and a solder bridge between them is the likely defect at this pitch. So no contact at a supply-rail potential has a neighbour in its row other than GND. (1) Rail contacts are the power contacts, the sense/supply taps and the rail nodes: crossing nets that a resistor below rail_node_max_ohm joins to a net other than GND, such as the 0.22 ohm damper nodes (BIAS_CH1_DAMP: R232 from BIAS_CH1, C235 47 uF to GND; pcb/prepare.py low_ohm_links). They sit on the odd row of J208, each followed by its GND return on the same row (rail, GND, rail, GND, ...; the return is the next contact, 0.5 mm away), in the order rail_order (until 11.11.2026 a checkerboard over both rows with the return in the same column; both keep GND beside every rail contact). (2) One GND guard contact follows the rail block in its row; the rails of rail_row_even (LAB5) start the even row the same way, and the signal nets follow them on the even row. (3) Each declared sense pair (at the potential of its rail) takes one column at the end of the strip, with a GND guard column before it. A bridge from a rail contact can then only short that rail to GND, where its protection (tools/assembly_data.py NET_CURRENT) acts; it cannot join two rails, a rail and a sense line, or a rail and a signal line. rail_order puts 3V3_Q6A first and the 12-13.8 V rails of the net names (the BONI13V8 tap, LNB13V2, AUX12 and BONI13V8_PORT) last; between them, for the PWR-B board of record, the rails that leave to the west (LNA4V5, the LNA bias dampers, E2_SB_DAMP, VBUS_RTLB_DAMP, VBUS_LABPORT), to the top edge (VBUS_HFP) and to the right (LAB5_RLY, BIAS_CH4_DAMP); the four LAB5 contacts sit on the even row (rail_row_even). The damper nodes also get their AC return beside them: the 47 uF capacitor sits on PWR-A and the 0.22 ohm resistor on PWR-B. Cost for (a): 10 GND contacts more than one per power contact (6 rail nodes, 1 tap, 3 guards). Design value; signal nets still neighbour signal nets

height_rule.rule: a PWR part goes to PWR-B only if its schematic group is in partition.PWR_B_groups and its read or class height (heights) is <= hB; otherwise it stays on PWR-A (DOMAIN_OVERRIDE). Every PWR-A part taller than hA gets a window in PWR-B (courtyard + window_margin each side); inside a window a PWR-A part may reach stack + board_t + hB = 12.1 mm
height_rule.pwr_b_header_rule: a PWR-B header takes the first family variant whose mated height is <= hB (side entry at hB 5.5); PWR-A headers sit in uncovered edge strips (courtyard + margin), because every one of them is taller than hA
height_rule.finding: at 72ee71b 17 THT radials with read heights (EEU-FR1H470 x15 11.2 mm, UHE1E221MPD C207 11.5 mm, EEU-FR1C101 C511 11.0 mm; LCSC via the JLCPCB search, read 2026-11-07) already exceed the PWR max_height 9.0 of mechanical/params/boards.json:28; the 18th radial C512 (EEU-FR1C221) has no read height (class 7.0 from the KiCad footprint, TBD).
